summary: The UNESCO/Poland Co-Sponsored Fellowships in Engineering are offered by the Polish National Commission for UNESCO and the UNESCO Chair for Science, Technology and Engineering at AGH University of Krakow. The 2025 edition offered 28 fellowships for an individual research programme of six months (1 October 2025 to 31 March 2026) in science, technology and engineering. Candidates come from 57 invited developing Member States and are endorsed by their National Commission for UNESCO. The edition is closed; no later edition was found on the UNESCO pages read.
eligibility_notes:
Nationality: citizens of the 57 invited Member States in Annex II: Africa (21), Arab States (2: Bahrain and Iraq), Asia and the Pacific (22) and Latin America and the Caribbean (12). Some projects are open only to candidates from certain regions (for example projects 05 and 06 only to Latin America and the Caribbean, project 07 to South-East Asia and the Pacific, project 08 to Africa).

Education: each of the 28 research projects names its own entry degree. Most need at least a B.Sc. in the named field; others need an M.Sc. (projects 02 and 03) or an M.Sc. or PhD (projects 14 and 15). You must also be a confirmed student, or a member of a research institution or university staff, for the whole period 1 October 2025 to 31 March 2026.

Age: not more than 32 years of age for most projects, and not more than 30 for projects 07 and 08.

Language: proficient reading and writing in English. A UNESCO language certificate is needed if English is not your mother tongue. Several geology projects (09, 10, 11) require you to bring your own samples to study.

Individuals cannot apply to UNESCO directly; only candidates endorsed by their National Commission for UNESCO are considered. Incomplete documents lead to rejection on formal grounds.
age_experience_notes: Age limit: not more than 32 years for most projects and not more than 30 for projects 07 and 08 (Annexes III and IV). Required skills differ per project (for example programming, laboratory work or geological sampling).
funding_summary: For six months the Polish side gives free tuition and access to university facilities, a monthly allowance of 1,800 PLN (BSc) or 2,200 PLN (MSc) meant to cover all living and accommodation costs, and a one-time arrival allowance of the same amount that covers a compulsory medical check-up and study-related visits, conferences, workshops and seminars. UNESCO pays international travel to and from Poland by the most direct economical route, health insurance for fellows declared medically fit, and a one-time pocket allowance of US$120. Passport and visa costs and the cost of family members are not covered.
programmes_note: Individual research programmes in science, technology and engineering, supervised by a tutor and coordinated by the UNESCO AGH Chair. Annex IV lists 28 projects in these disciplines: Biomedical Engineering; Computer and Information Sciences; Earth and Related Environmental Sciences; Environmental Engineering, Mining and Energy; Materials Engineering; Mechanical Engineering; Sociology. Each project has a set number of places (Annex III table shows 39 positions in total). Projects are split between the bachelor and master levels below by the minimum degree each asks for.
institutions_note: AGH University of Krakow, through the UNESCO AGH Chair for Science, Technology and Engineering. Each project is assigned to a tutor at AGH; candidates choose a project from Annex IV and apply for it.

application_steps.title: Check the terms, countries and projects
application_steps.detail: Read the terms and conditions (Annex I) and the list of fields and projects (Annex IV), and check that your country is among the 57 invited Member States (Annex II) and that you meet the entry degree and age limit of the project you want (Annex III).

application_steps.title: Contact your National Commission for UNESCO
application_steps.detail: Ask your National Commission about its national procedure. UNESCO does not accept individual applications; only candidates endorsed by their Commission are considered. The Commission sends the endorsement letter and scanned documents by email to the programme address.

application_steps.title: Prepare the documents and complete the online sheet
application_steps.detail: Prepare the four-page form in capital letters, passport and photo copies, certified degree copies with Apostille or legalisation, a language certificate if needed, and two recommendation letters dated 2025. After endorsement, complete the online information sheet. The page gave Monday 26 May 2025 (midnight, Paris time) as the Commission's deadline; Annex I says 12 May 2025.

application_steps.title: National selection by your Commission
application_steps.detail: National Commissions choose their candidates and send their endorsement letters and documents to UNESCO. Late or incomplete applications are not considered.

application_steps.title: Final selection by the Polish authorities
application_steps.detail: The Polish authorities make the final selection, with attention to gender equality and diversity. UNESCO tells the National Commissions which fellows were chosen; only selected candidates are notified, through their Commissions.

application_steps.title: Visa and travel
application_steps.detail: Selected fellows obtain their own Polish entry visa before departure, from a Polish embassy or consulate in their country or the nearest one, at their own cost. UNESCO pays the international travel to and from Poland.

application_steps.title: Six-month research stay at AGH University of Krakow
application_steps.detail: The stay runs 1 October 2025 to 31 March 2026 with a tutor at AGH. Fellows receive the monthly allowance and arrival allowance from the Polish authorities and take the compulsory medical check-up on arrival. UNESCO provides health insurance for fellows declared medically fit.

application_steps.title: Reports and certificate
application_steps.detail: At the end of the research stay fellows receive a certificate of attendance at the host institution. It is issued after the requested reports are received and financial clearance is given by the institution.

notes: This is the 2025 edition (closed). The stored cycle title says 2025 and the period is 1 October 2025 to 31 March 2026; treat as past unless a later edition appears.
The programme page gives Monday 26 May 2025 as the deadline for National Commissions; Annex I gives 12 May 2025.
The page says 28 fellowships; the Annex III summary table counts 28 projects and 39 positions in total (the maximum number of places per project adds up to 39). Both are given as stated.

Annex III and Annex IV give different titles for project 02 (Annex III: 'human body activity in stress conditions'; Annex IV: 'human emotional response to a visual stimulus'). The Annex III title is used.
Project 03: Annex III asks for an M.Sc.; the Annex IV table says B.Sc. or M.Sc. It is placed at master level.

The stored statement 'BSc and MSc students are named in the benefits' is replaced by the project-level entry degrees from Annex III. Stored nationality list (57 entries) is carried over from stored data; Annex II also lists 57 Member States.
